result.title: Confine to the Task, Anchor the Rest: Concept-Guided Retention Regularizer for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
result.summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has been widely used, yet the adapted model suffers catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge. While most existing work hardens the adapter by constraining where the weight update may lie, we note that constraining this weight channel does not constrain the activation channel. In this paper, we propose Concept-Guided Retention (CGR), a plug-and-play regularizer that constrains both for any PEFT base. CGR reads a frozen sparse autoencoder (SAE) and treats two disjoint concept sets differently. It softly confines the update to the task-concept subspace (via weight channel), and anchors a selected set of general-purpose concepts to the frozen model (via activation channel). We also provide anchor value bounds based on weight updates to understand how they interact, and show that both terms are necessary. On a CLIP vision panel, CGR significantly improves retention at comparable accuracy for every base, and the same pattern holds for world-knowledge retention under Llama-3.1-8B instruction tuning. Because the protected directions are named SAE concepts, CGR remains inspectable and controllable.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Concept-Guided Retention（CGR），一个即插即用的 PEFT 正则化器：借助冻结的稀疏自编码器读取概念，用权重通道把更新软约束到任务概念子空间，并用激活通道把选定的通用概念锚定到原模型，在 CLIP 视觉面板与 Llama-3.1-8B 指令微调上验证保留效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「激活通道 + SAE 概念子空间」约束线索可能可供核查：在训练 latent 推理状态时，是否可用类似概念级正则抑制任务必要视觉信息在微调中的坍缩或流失，但该文关注的是通用知识保留而非推理状态生成。
